summary: Steel Aermotor tower built near Schuylkill County Airport; moved off its hill, its top section and cab now stand at Owl Creek Recreation Area in Tamaqua.

facts.design: Steel Aermotor tower with a cab
facts.status_note: Moved from its original site on Mount Pleasant; the top section and cab stand at Owl Creek Recreation Area in Tamaqua.

access.note: A 2013 report said the tower would be open during hayrides and special events at Owl Creek; no later hours were found.

events.note: The register gives 1921; a 2015 newspaper gives 1920 and a 2013 report says only 'the 1920s'
Emma Lord, appointed a fire warden, was placed in charge of the tower
Mrs. Vernie Ringenary in charge at the tower
County commissioners approved an agreement letting the county install an antenna on the tower
Listed on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register as US 388, PA 217
Top section and cab set up at Owl Creek Recreation Area in Tamaqua; the 85-foot tower had earlier been moved to the DCNR Weiser District office in Cressona
Restored by volunteers of South Ward Fire Company, Tamaqua; shown at Owl Creek for the 100th anniversary of the Pennsylvania Forest Fire Wardens

corrections.why: The register gives the county as Schuylkill County. The record's spelling is a typo.
30.5 m matches the 1923 newspaper's 100 feet. The 2013 and 2015 reports describe the tower near the airport as 85 feet (25.9 m).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the tower was removed in the mid-1990s; a 2015 report says DCNR dismantled it in the late 1990s before moving it to Cressona. The story gives both.
The register gives 1921, a 2015 newspaper gives 1920, and a 2013 report says only 'the 1920s'. The story gives the register's year and notes the others.
A 1923 newspaper gave 100 feet; the 2013 and 2015 reports give 85 feet for the tower as it stood near the airport. The story uses 85 feet.

notes_for_editor: The history from 1921 to 2015 agrees on the Owl Creek move (August 2013) and the 2015 restoration, but the build year (1920 or 1921) and the height (100 or 85 feet) disagree. The 1923 newspaper gives 100 feet; the 2013 and 2015 reports give 85. The brief's county spelling, 'Schuykill', is a typo; the register spells it Schuylkill. The eastern lookouts page and the 2013 and 2015 articles are reprints or local news, not primary records, and we did not check the originals. The newest source is August 2015; no source says whether the tower is open today. The tower's exact height at Owl Creek is not given.
